label: Mdef:matrixmaj
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{Mdef:matrixmaj}
Fix $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and consider collections $P=\left(p^{(1)},\ldots,p^{(d)}\right)$ and $Q=\left(q^{(1)},\ldots,q^{(d)}\right)$ of probability vectors. We say that $P$ majorizes $Q$ and denote $P\succeq Q$ if there is a stochastic map $T$ such that $Tp^{(k)}=q^{(k)}$ for $k=1,\ldots,d$. We call this form of majorization {\it matrix majorization}.

title: Proposition
body_md: All homomorphisms in $\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d,\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})$ are monotone.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\underline{\alpha}\in\mathbb{R}_+^d$ such that $\alpha_1+\ldots+\alpha_d=1$, and $C\in\mathcal{P}([d])\setminus\emptyset$ such that $C$ contains all columns $c$ with $\alpha_c\neq0$. Consider $P\in\mathcal{V}_n^d$ with rows $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in\mathbb{R}_+^d$ and a stochastic $m\times n$-matrix $T$, and write $Q:=TP\in\mathcal{V}_m^d$ with rows $q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb{R}_+^d$, and $T_i:=\sum_{j=1}^n T_{i,j}>0$. Using the concavity of $\varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}$ in the first inequality, we find 
\begin{align}
\Phi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(Q)&=\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}\varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(q_i)\\
&=\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}\varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}\left(\sum_{j=1}^n T_{i,j}p_j\right)=\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}T_i\varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}\left(\sum_{j=1}^n \frac{T_{i,j}}{T_i}p_j\right)\\
&\geq\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}T_i\sum_{j=1}^n \frac{T_{i,j}}{T_i}\varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(p_j)=\sum_{j=1}^n \varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(p_j)\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}T_{i,j}\\
&=\sum_{j\in I(P,C)} \varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(p_j)\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}T_{i,j}}_{=1}+\sum_{j\notin I(P,C)} \varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(p_j)\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}T_{i,j}\\
&\geq\sum_{j\in I(P,C)} \varphi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(p_j)=\Phi_{\underline{\alpha},C}(P). 
\end{align}
To see why $\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}T_{i,j}=1$ for all $j\in I(P,C)$, consider any $j\in I(P,C)$ and $i\notin I(Q,C)$. Then there exists a column $k\in C$ such that $\sum_{j^\prime=1}^n T_{i,j^\prime}(p_{j^\prime})_k=0$, hence $T_{i,j}(p_j)_k=0$. Since $j\in I(P,C)$ implies that $(p_j)_k>0$, we conclude that $T_{i,j}=0$. This means that $\sum_{i\in I(Q,C)}T_{i,j}=\sum_{i=1}^m T_{i,j}=1$ for all $j\in I(P,C)$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Mpro:monhommin}
The non-degenerate monotone homomorphisms $S^d\rightarrow\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op}$ are exactly those in $\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d,\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})$. For $\mathbb{K}$ equal to $\mathbb{R}_+$, $\mathbb{T}\mathbb{R}_+$ or $\mathbb{T}\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op}$, there are no non-degenerate monotone homomorphisms $S^d\rightarrow\mathbb{K}$.

label: Mlem:poweruniversalconditions
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{Mlem:poweruniversalconditions}
		Let $U=(u^{(1)},\ldots,u^{(d)})\in \mathcal{V}^d$ with $u^{(k)}$ for $k\in[d]$ probability distributions. Then the following are equivalent: 
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item $U$ is power universal. 
			\item There exists $m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $k\in[d]$, $U^{\boxtimes m}$ has a row $(0\,\cdots\,0\underbrace{x_k}_{k\text{-th entry}}0\,\cdots\,0)$ for some $x_k>0$. 
			\item It holds that ${\rm supp}\,u^{(k)}\nsubseteq{\rm supp}\,u^{(k^\prime)}$ for all $k,k^\prime\in[d]$, $k\neq k^\prime$. 
			\item Any nondegenerate homomorphism $\Phi\in\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d,\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})$ satisfies $\Phi(U)<1$. 
		\end{enumerate}

label: Mthm:minimal
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{Mthm:minimal}
     Let $O$ be a non-empty open subset of $\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d,\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})$. There exist tuples of probability vectors $P=(p^{(1)},\ldots,p^{(d)})$, $Q=(q^{(1)},\ldots,q^{(d)})$ such that $\bigcap_{k=1}^d{\rm supp}\,p^{(k)}\neq\emptyset$ and $\bigcap_{k=1}^d{\rm supp}\,q^{(k)}\neq\emptyset$, $P$ is power universal, and such that \eqref{Meq:majorizationconditions} holds for all $\Phi_{\underline{\alpha},C}\in\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d,\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})\setminus O$, but both (a) and (b) of Theorem \ref{Mthm:majorization} do not hold. Additionally, in Theorem \ref{Mthm:genasymptocatalytic}, \eqref{Meq:genasymptocatalyticcondition} holds for all continuous $\Phi_{\underline{\alpha},C}\in\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d,\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})\setminus O$ \footnote{Note that any non-empty open $O\subseteq\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d,\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})$ contains some continuous homomorphisms.}, but both (ii) and (iii) do not hold.

title: Proposition
body_md: All homomorphisms in $\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d_{\rm d.c.},\mathbb{R}_+)$ are monotone.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\alpha>1$ and $c\in[d-1]$. Consider $P\in S^d_{\rm d.c.}$ with rows $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in\mathbb{R}_+^d$ and a stochastic $m\times n$-matrix $T$, and write $Q:=TP\in S^d_{\rm d.c.}$ with rows $q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb{R}_+^d$, and $T_i:=\sum_{j=1}^n T_{i,j}>0$. Using the convexity of $\varphi_{\alpha,c}$ and the fact that $\left(p_j\right)_d>0$ for all $j\in[n]$, we find 
		\begin{align}
			\Phi_{\alpha,c}(Q)&=\sum_{i=1}^m\varphi_{\alpha,c}(q_i)=\sum_{i=1}^m\varphi_{\alpha,c}\left(\sum_{j=1}^n T_{i,j}p_j\right)\\
            &=\sum_{i=1}^m T_i\varphi_{\alpha,c}\left(\sum_{j=1}^n \frac{T_{i,j}}{T_i}p_j\right)\leq\sum_{i=1}^m T_i\sum_{j=1}^n \frac{T_{i,j}}{T_i}\varphi_{\alpha,c}(p_j)\\
            &=\sum_{j=1}^n \varphi_{\alpha,c}(p_j)\underbrace{\sum_{i=1}^m T_{i,j}}_{=1}=\Phi_{\alpha,c}(P), 
		\end{align}
		which completes the proof.

title: Remark
body_md: Note that, compared to the minimally restricted semiring $S^d$, some elements in $\mathcal{H}^{\rm n.d.}(S^d_{\rm d.c.},\mathbb{R}_+^{\rm op})$ coincide. Since the final column dominates all the other columns in all matrices in $\mathcal{V}^d_{\rm d.c.}$, it immediately follows that, whenever $\underline{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{d-1},0)\in A_+$ and ${\rm supp}\,\underline{\alpha}\subseteq C\subseteq[d]$, we have $\Phi_{\underline{\alpha},C}=\Phi_{\underline{\alpha},C\cup\{d\}}$. See also Figure \ref{Mfig:DominatingColumn} for a depiction of the monotone homomorphisms in the case $d=3$. The figure also shows the derivations which we study in the next subsection.

title: Remark
body_md:
We may derive an asymptotic version of this result, analogous to Theorem \ref{Mthm:genasymptocatalytic}. However, we would have to require the matrix $P$ to be power universal, which according to the characterization in (ii) of Proposition \ref{Mpro:poweruniversaldcgeneral} is quite restrictive. Nevertheless, for the case $d=2$, the situation is manageable, since there are essentially three interesting cases: either both columns have the same support and are different, or both columns have part of the support outside of the support of the other column, or one column has support strictly contained in the other. Majorization results (both for the exact and asymptotic setting) for the first case were derived in \cite{farooq2024}, and the second case is covered by the results in subsection \ref{Msubsec:applyingvssnorestrictions}. The third case is covered by Theorem \ref{Mthm:majorizationdominatingcolumn} (for the exact setting) above and by Theorem \ref{Mthm:asymptocatalytic} (for the asymptotic setting) in the next section, where we will derive an analogue of Theorem \ref{Mthm:genasymptocatalytic} for the case $d=2$. 
        
        Note that for $d>2$ there are many possibilities for the relationships of the supports of the columns, and each would require a different semiring to be studied. We will discuss this issue further in Section \ref{Msec:pusupports}.

label: thm:LS
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:LS}
    Let $(\rho,\sigma)$, $(\rho',\sigma')$ be two pairs of states in $\mathcal{F}$, where additionally $(\rho,\sigma)$ satisfies \eqref{eq:pu2}. If 
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:LScondition1}&\hat{D}_{\alpha,z}(\rho\|\sigma)>\hat{D}_{\alpha,z}(\rho'\|\sigma')\ \text{when}\ \alpha\in[0,1],\ z\geq\max\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}, &\\
        \label{eq:LScondition2}&\hat{D}^\mathbb{T}(\rho\|\sigma)>\hat{D}^\mathbb{T}(\rho'\|\sigma'), 
    \end{align}            
    then $(\rho,\sigma)$ majorizes $(\rho',\sigma')$ both in the large-sample setting and in the catalytic setting, with a pair of catalyst states in $\mathcal{F}$. For the catalytic result, $(\rho,\sigma)$ does not need to satisfy \eqref{eq:pu2}. 
    
    Conversely, if $(\rho,\sigma)$ majorizes $(\rho',\sigma')$ in large samples or catalytically, then the above inequalities \eqref{eq:LScondition1} and \eqref{eq:LScondition2} hold non-strictly.
